known_limitations: The same method and sources are applied to all sites. Climate comes from a global gridded product (NASA POWER/MERRA-2, ≈50 km); very local extremes such as the hyperaridity of La Pampa de la Joya may be overestimated. No site-specific corrections are applied.

The lunar target square (10 × 10 km around LOLA Site 04, Shackleton rim) includes part of the crater's inner wall (≈4 km of relief), so its mean slope is high; it represents the terrain surrounding a possible base, not only the flat rim.
Temperatures are adjusted to the site elevation with a standard lapse rate (6.5 °C/km).
Slope and roughness depend on DEM resolution; all bodies are compared at ≈30 m.
Planetary temperature ranges are published reference values, not computed from rasters.

similarity_method.description: Weighted average of partial scores (0-100). Slope, roughness and temperature range: ratio smaller/larger value. Aridity: exp(-P/200 mm).

jezero.name: Jezero crater — Perseverance landing site
jezero.notes: Temperature range = mid-point of the 50–60 °C daily air-temperature variation reported from Perseverance/MEDA. No liquid precipitation on Mars (0 mm).

lunar-south-pole.name: Lunar south pole — Shackleton rim (LOLA Site 04)
lunar-south-pole.notes: Temperature range = +22 °C to −220 °C reported by NASA for candidate south-pole landing sites (surface temperature; the Moon has no air). No precipitation (0 mm).
